A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FDHO research work. Their main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original signal, audio, image and reconstruction experiments, including the Adaptive SIREN comparison and supplementary SDF and Poisson results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds matched training controls, initialization sensitivity, compatibility experiments and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The FDHO activation, shared oscillator parameters, training objective and default procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. The compatibility experiments reuse the existing activation; the alternative Poisson initialization is an experimental variant.

E1.justification: Section D.2 adds a carphone video-fitting example using ResFields, extending coverage to spatiotemporal video. A Kodak Image 07 example supplements existing image fitting. All earlier tasks remain, and the added coverage consists of individual compatibility examples.

E2.justification: v3 adds TUNER, SASNet and SAPE to the Tiger comparison in Table 15. Adaptive SIREN, previously evaluated on the toy signal, also participates in Tiger and CT controls. New compatibility tests compare SIREN and FDHO activations within FreSh and ResFields. The original eight benchmark baselines remain.

E3.justification: New Section C.2 matches architecture at m=256 and L=5 and uses Adam with learning rate 10^-4 for both weights and activation parameters, without a scheduler. Section D.2 separately tests Poisson initialization with omega_0=15 instead of 45, retaining omega_n,0=50. These additional protocols do not replace the original experiment settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing whether the advantage persists with matched architecture and optimizer settings on Tiger and CT, an initialization sensitivity test for Poisson reconstruction, and FreSh/ResFields compatibility cases. The existing toy-signal dynamics analysis and computational-cost comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are averaged over 10 runs and retain the explicit single-run exception for SDF fitting. Existing uncertainty reporting is unchanged; additional result entries do not introduce new statistical procedures, significance tests or increased run counts.

E6.justification: All original table values are retained. New Table 11 reports FDHO final Tiger PSNR of 63.27±1.30 dB and CT PSNR of 40.16±0.46 dB under the control protocol; Table 15 adds baseline scores. Section D.2 adds the Poisson initialization result of 30.11±0.64 dB and SIREN/FDHO compatibility results of 30.32/34.39 dB for FreSh and 28.4/35.47 dB for ResFields. These are additional experiments, not revisions of the original results.

T1.justification: The activation definition, propositions, theorems, corollaries and derivations in Section 3 and Appendix A are retained. Matching the equations across reflow shows no substantive mathematical additions or corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims: oscillator-based activation, implicit spectral gating, coarse-to-fine learning and competitive performance without task-specific tuning. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 attributes the matched-control advantages to the activation formulation and adds explicit compatibility claims for FreSh and ResFields. Section 4.1 also interprets existing run variability as evidence of a more robust optimization landscape. Earlier qualifications concerning inpainting, regular textures and Poisson supervision remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the architecture, common learning rate and absence of scheduling for the new controls, the alternative Poisson initialization, and activation substitution in the compatibility tests. Appendix B configurations, hardware and timing information, and project/code-release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to TUNER, SASNet, SAPE, FreSh and ResFields. Section 2 explicitly positions FDHO's training-dependent gating against TUNER's initialization-based spectral control. This expands the existing positioning without substantially restructuring it.

P1.justification: There are localized related-work rewrites, added explanatory paragraphs, a new control-study subsection, paragraphing adjustments and a funding footnote. Most prose and the overall main-text and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 11 and 15; the earlier appendix Tables 11–13 become Tables 12–14. Tables and figures move with reflow, and several raster figures have lower resolution while retaining their displayed content. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The matched optimizer controls in Section C.2 address a comparison concern left by v1's different FDHO learning rates and scheduling. Additional baselines and the Poisson sensitivity test strengthen empirical support, while the TUNER discussion improves positioning. The gain is limited by the selected-example coverage and brief compatibility protocols; some figures also lose raster resolution. The core method, theory and original benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
